name: Environment Configuration Conventions
description: This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing environment configuration code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing environment configuration style guide.
content:
This module defines the naming, formatting, and structural style conventions to follow whenever writing, implementing, or reviewing environment configuration code or output, so results stay consistent with the existing environment configuration style guide.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. When environment configuration guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
2. State assumptions about environment configuration explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
3. Keep environment configuration changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
4. Re-check edge cases relevant to environment configuration (empty input, boundary values, concurrent access) before calling the task done.
5. Validate environment configuration outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
6. Document any non-obvious environment configuration decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
7. Surface known limitations of a chosen environment configuration approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
8. Before starting environment configuration work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
9. Measure before optimizing any environment configuration bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated environment configuration concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Avoid introducing new environment configuration abstractions before there is a second concrete use case that needs them.
- Do not skip documenting environment configuration assumptions just because they seem obvious in the moment.

CLOSING NOTE
These guidelines are a starting point for environment configuration, not an exhaustive rulebook — use judgment when a rule doesn't fit the situation.
